newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nervy Brussels bourse to eye U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Nervy Brussels bourse to eye U.S. jobs data.

text.p: U.S. jobless claims figures due on Thursday when Belgian markets are closed will provide the key to the performance of a nervy Brussels bourse when it opens on a holiday-thinned Friday, traders said on Wednesday.

"If the figures are good the market could rise a bit. If they are bad it could fall, but not far as the market is well supported," one trader said. "But it risks being volatile because many people are also taking Friday off."
The Bel-20 share index ended a yo-yoing Wednesday up 10.53 points or 0.47 percent at a closing high of 2,245.51. More than three billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands.
Latest U.S. jobless data for April are expected to show a figure of 325,000.
Traders said the Brussels bourse would also be edgy on Friday because of the closure of markets in the United States and Britain on Monday for a bank holiday.
They said the bourse panicked briefly on Wednesday after very strong U.S. first quarter growth figures, but had then reconsidered and recovered -- as had New York when it opened.
"High growth is good news if there is no inflation," one trader said.

Traders said Wednesday's trading had been epitomised by buying of stocks soon to go ex-dividend -- such as Electrabel, which was the busiest stock by value -- and continued interest in the banking sector.
Apart from isolated cases such as non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere and oil major PetroFina there were no other specific areas of interest, they said.
Electrabel, which will pay out net dividend of 352 francs per share on May 28 if its May 12 annual meeting approves, ended 0.7 percent up at 8,120 francs with 50,000 shares traded.
Banque Bruxelles Lambert rose 0.9 percent to 8,930 francs, Generale Bank added 0.5 percent to 14,825 francs.
But Kredietbank lost 1.2 percent to 13,925 francs on profit-taking after climbing three percent on Tuesday.
The banking sector has been leading the Brussels bourse higher all this week.
Union Miniere was the strongest gainer, rising 2.7 percent to 2,905 francs. Traders said the rise followed a relatively weak performance on Tuesday.
PetroFina, which Generale Bank rated a 'buy', rose 1.8 percent to 12,725 francs.
It was the second busiest stock by value with more than 22,000 shares changing hands.
At the other end of the scale steel cord and wire maker Bekaert lost 3.8 percent to 21,425 francs in what traders said was a technical correction.
